images.title: Finding 45° and 135°
images.purpose: Show that one fold part of a semicircle is 45° and the rest is 180° − 45° = 135°.
images.composition: One large semicircle centred with the equation line centred below it.
images.exact_structure: One semicircle with its straight edge at the bottom, divided by exactly 3 grey #6B7280 creases from the centre into 4 equal wedges of 45° each. The wedge next to the right end is filled teal #0072B2; the other 3 wedges together are filled amber #E69F00. Exactly 1 semicircle, 4 equal wedges, 1 equation line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
wedges that are not equal in size
images.takeaway: A semicircle of 180° splits into 45° and 135°.
images.description: A semicircle in four equal wedges with one wedge shaded teal as 45° and the other three shaded amber as 135°.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the 45° wedge, then at the 135° part, and say what they add up to.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
